report.source_text: A PRBC transfusion was administered as the initial treatment, following which oral prednisone was administered at a dose of 2 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks and then tapered slowly. The patient was continued on maintenance oral prednisone at a dose of 0.3 mg/kg on alternate days and has since been observed to sustain a hemoglobin level of >9.0 g/dL without receiving further transfusions. As an operative repair of the CDH was not performed at the time, a follow-up of the condition was planned on outpatient basis.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Diamond-Blackfan Anemia (DBA) due to heterozygous RPS19 gene mutation c.380G>A (p.Gly127Glu)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-month-old male with prenatal diagnosis of hydrops fetalis presented with severe neonatal anemia requiring 6 packed red blood cell transfusions in the first month and continued transfusion dependence until 3 months of age. He achieved apparent remission with hemoglobin >9.0 g/dL from 4 months until recurrence of severe anemia at 19 months (hemoglobin 5.4 g/dL). Laboratory evaluation revealed macrocytic anemia (MCV 105.9 fL), inappropriately low reticulocyte count (0.9%), elevated hemoglobin F (12.1%), and markedly elevated erythrocyte adenosine deaminase (60.2 IU/L). Bone marrow examination showed selective erythroid hypoplasia with markedly decreased erythropoietic cells and elevated myeloid-to-erythroid ratio (18:1), while myeloid and megakaryocytic lineages remained normal. Genetic analysis confirmed heterozygous RPS19 mutation c.380G>A (p.Gly127Glu), establishing the diagnosis of Diamond-Blackfan anemia. Treatment with prednisone (initial 2 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks, then tapered to 0.3 mg/kg on alternate days) resulted in sustained hemoglobin >9.0 g/dL without further transfusions. Associated features included growth restriction, developmental delay, congenital cataract, strabismus, Bochdalek hernia, and recurrent respiratory infections. Family history was significant for an older male sibling who died of apnea at 5 months.
